evidence.description: The timer directly accesses Statistics.shared to obtain its operating interval.
treesAt directly reads the singleton's statistics to calculate its result.

candidates.explanation: TreesProjection directly obtains application statistics from Statistics.shared rather than receiving the service through an explicit, replaceable dependency boundary.
candidates.title: Direct Singleton Service Access

evidence.description: The task is stored on the owner, then weak self is promoted to a strong local reference before entering the repeating loop that uses it.
The only visible cancellation occurs in deinit, which the retained owner cannot reach while the task continues.

candidates.explanation: The object stores a repeating task that retains it for the duration of the loop. Although the initial capture is weak, the guard promotes self to a strong reference before the loop, and that reference remains live across iterations. Cancellation only in deinit cannot break this ownership cycle because the task prevents deallocation.
candidates.title: Task Ownership Retain Cycle
